name: Shebaniah
title: Levite and Teacher of the Law After the Exile
summary: Shebaniah was a Levite who played an important role in Israel's rebuilding after the Babylonian exile. He was known for his insight into God's law and served as a leader among the Levites under Ezra and Nehemiah. He actively participated in the reading of the Law, worship, and covenant renewal in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Arrival with Ezra from Babylon
keyEvents.description: Shebaniah was among the Levites who joined Ezra at the Ahava River before the journey to Jerusalem. Ezra describes him as a wise man.

keyEvents.title: Guardians of Temple Gifts
keyEvents.description: Shebaniah was entrusted with the responsibility of guarding the silver, gold, and holy vessels that were to be transported to the temple in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Reading of the Law at the Square
keyEvents.description: Shebaniah was among the Levites who helped the people understand the Law when Ezra read it aloud to the crowd in front of the Water Gate.

keyEvents.title: Prayer and Praise During the Fast
keyEvents.description: Shebania led the people in prayer and praise during a great day of fasting, where the people confessed their sins and the sins of their fathers.

keyEvents.title: The Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Shebania was among the Levites who put their seal on the covenant, where the people committed themselves to keeping God's law and commandments.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Song of Praise
keyEvents.description: Shebania served among the Levites who led thanksgiving and praise at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
